item.title: Best Bars in Collingwood 2026: Smith Street and Beyond
item.description:
Best Bars in Collingwood 2026: Smith Street and Beyond

Collingwood’s bar scene runs on the same energy as the suburb itself — a little rough around the edges, completely unpretentious, and absolutely refusing to be anything it’s not. Smith Street has been Melbourne’s bar corridor for well over a decade now, and in 2026 it’s still delivering. But the real magic happens when you duck off the main strip into the side streets and laneways where the proper joints live.

item.title: Collingwood Cost of Living 2026: Real Prices, Real Talk
item.description:
Updated 16 March 2026 | Marcus Cole reporting

Collingwood in 2026 is the suburb Melbourne can’t stop arguing about. Half the city swears it’s still the cheap, gritty inner-north option. The other half just paid $650 a week for a one-bedroom on Smith Street and is quietly having a crisis.

The truth, as usual, sits somewhere in the middle — but it’s creeping closer to “expensive” with every quarter. Collingwood’s cost of living has shifted noticeably since 2024, and if you’re thinking about moving here, already here, or just trying to figure out whether your pay rise actually kept up with your rent, this is the article for you.

item.title: Collingwood Honest Guide 2026: Smith Street & Real Talk
item.description:
Collingwood Honest Guide 2026: Smith Street & Real Talk

Updated 16 March 2026 | Jack Morrison reporting

Collingwood is the suburb that Melbourne’s real estate agents love to describe as “gritty” in their listings, then price like it’s inner-city Toorak. It’s the place where a $6 flat white sits next to a $350,000 warehouse conversion, where a tattooed sommelier pours natural wine in a room that still smells faintly of its industrial past, and where nobody — absolutely nobody — uses the phrase “bohemian charm” without being politely asked to leave.
